chapters.title: Chapter 1: Why Real Estate Valuation Matters

lessons.title: What Valuing a Property Actually Means: Price, Value and the Gap Between Them

children.text: Ravi is selling a 2BHK flat in Wakad, Pune. In the same week, four different numbers show up for the exact same flat. The Maharashtra ready reckoner puts it at ₹78 lakh for stamp duty purposes. His broker tells him he can list it at ₹98 lakh, based on what two similar flats in the building sold for last month. The bank's registered valuer, sent to check the property before sanctioning the buyer's loan, assesses it at ₹86 lakh. And after two weeks of back and forth, Ravi and the buyer settle at ₹90 lakh. One flat. Four numbers. This lesson explains why that happens, and which number you should actually trust, and when.

body.text: Price is what someone actually paid or is willing to pay in one specific deal. Value is what a defensible, repeatable method says an asset is worth. The two are related, but they are not the same thing, and confusing them is how investors overpay, underinsure, and lose arguments with banks.

children.text: Price is a fact about one transaction. It is set by whatever the buyer was willing to pay and the seller was willing to accept, on that specific day, under those specific conditions. Price absorbs everything that has nothing to do with the property itself: how urgently the seller needed cash, how attached the buyer was to a particular school district, how many other buyers were bidding, whether the broker inflated the asking figure to leave room for negotiation. None of that changes what the flat is actually worth. It only changes what one buyer paid one seller.

markDefs.definition: A professional empanelled with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) under the Land and Building asset class, authorised to issue formal valuation reports for purposes such as insolvency proceedings, company law and dispute resolution.

children.text: Value is an opinion, but a disciplined one. A valuer estimates it by applying a defined method (comparable sales, income capitalization, or replacement cost, the three you will learn in this course) to verifiable inputs: what similar properties actually sold for, what rent the property can actually command, what it would actually cost to rebuild. For formal purposes, such as insolvency proceedings, company mergers, or a contested family settlement, Indian practice increasingly requires this opinion to come from a
, working to a written methodology that can be defended in front of a bank, a tribunal, or a court.

body.label: Who can issue a formal valuation report
body.context: Required for several company, insolvency and regulatory purposes under the Companies (Registered Valuers and Valuation) Rules, 2017. Banks separately empanel their own valuers for loan purposes.

children.text: Why Price and Value Pull Apart

body.title: What Pushes Price Away From Value

columns.label: Pushes price above value
points: An emotionally attached buyer who has fallen for this specific flat
Genuine scarcity, only one unit available in a preferred society
A broker's asking figure inflated to leave room for negotiation
A buyer who is missing information about defects or a weak title

columns.label: Pushes price below value
points: A distress sale, the seller needs cash urgently
A pending title dispute or unresolved litigation
Negative sentiment across the local market
A seller unaware of the property's real rental or resale potential

children.text: One Flat, Four Numbers: Ravi's Wakad Example

body.title: Show me: why Ravi's flat had four different numbers

children.text: Each of the four numbers from the opening was doing a different job. None of them was wrong. They were simply answering different questions.

cells: What is the minimum value for stamp duty and registration?
What could this fetch if we find an eager buyer?
An empanelled valuer following a written method
What can the bank safely lend against?
Ravi and the buyer, after negotiation
What did this specific deal actually settle at?

children.text: Notice that the transacted price, ₹90 lakh, sits between the broker's optimistic asking figure and the bank valuer's more conservative estimate. That pattern is common. Asking prices are opening bids dressed up as facts. A valuer's report is closer to a defensible floor.

body.text: The number that matters depends on what you are doing. Paying stamp duty: the circle rate. Getting a loan: the bank's valuer. Actually buying or selling: the negotiated price. Settling an estate or a dispute: a registered valuer's report. Using the wrong number for the wrong job is a common, expensive mistake.

children.text: Why This Distinction Matters for You

If you are buying, the broker's asking price tells you almost nothing about whether you are overpaying. If you are borrowing, the bank lends against its valuer's number, not your negotiated price, so a wide gap between the two can leave you scrambling for extra margin money. If you are an angel investor accepting property as collateral, or an HNI settling a family property dispute, a defensible valuation is the only thing that holds up when someone challenges the number later. Sentiment fades. A properly documented method survives scrutiny.

body.text: Banks calculate loan-to-value on whichever is lower: your agreement value or the registered valuer's assessed value. If Ravi's buyer needed a loan, the bank would lend against ₹86 lakh, not the ₹90 lakh he actually agreed to pay, leaving him to fund the ₹4 lakh gap from his own pocket.

children.text: Every registered valuer reaches their number using one of three defensible methods: pricing a property against what comparable properties recently sold for, pricing it against the income it can generate, or pricing it against what it would cost to rebuild today. The next lesson looks at who actually needs a real estate valuation and why. Lesson 3 in this chapter maps all three methods before you go deep on each one, starting with comparable sales in Chapter 2.

body.title: Quick Check: Price or Value?
body.question: A broker tells a seller she can list her flat at ₹1.1 crore because a similar unit two floors up recently sold for that amount. Is this number price or value?
options: It is value, because it is based on a comparable sale
It is price, an asking figure dressed up as fact, until a buyer actually agrees to it
It is both, since comparable sales are one of the three valuation methods
Neither, since no method was used at all
body.explanation: An asking price is an opinion about what the market might bear, not a completed transaction and not a disciplined valuation. It becomes a price only when a buyer actually pays it, and it would only count as a defensible value if it followed a proper comparable sales method with several verified, adjusted comparables, not a single anecdote from two floors up.

body.title: Scenario: The Loan Shortfall
body.scenario: Meera agrees to buy a flat in Noida for ₹75 lakh. She applies for a home loan expecting 80% financing, or ₹60 lakh. The bank's registered valuer assesses the flat at ₹68 lakh, well below the agreed price, citing a recent oversupply of similar units nearby.
body.prompt: How much will the bank actually lend, and what should Meera do?
body.modelAnswer: Banks lend against the lower of the agreement value and the valuer's assessed value. Here that is ₹68 lakh, so at an 80% LTV the bank sanctions roughly ₹54.4 lakh, about ₹5.6 lakh less than Meera expected. She can renegotiate the price with the seller using the valuer's report as leverage, arrange the shortfall from her own funds, or request a second valuation if she has genuine grounds to believe the first one under-assessed the property, for instance if the valuer missed a recent renovation or used stale comparables.

cards.definition: What was or would be paid in a specific transaction; shaped by negotiation, urgency and sentiment as much as by the asset itself.
The most probable price a property should command in a competitive, open market, estimated using a defined valuation method.
A professional empanelled with the IBBI under the Land and Building asset class, authorised to issue valuation reports for formal purposes such as insolvency, company law and dispute resolution.
The government-notified minimum value per unit area used to calculate stamp duty; a floor for tax purposes, not a market estimate.
The percentage of a property's assessed value that a bank is willing to lend, calculated on whichever is lower: the agreement value or the valuer's assessed value.

points: Price is what one buyer paid one seller in a specific deal; value is an estimate produced by a defined, repeatable method.

The same property can carry several legitimate numbers at once: circle rate for stamp duty, an asking price, a bank valuer's assessment, and the final transacted price, each answering a different question.
Formal valuations for insolvency, company law or dispute purposes generally require an IBBI-registered valuer working to a documented method.
Banks lend against the lower of the agreement value and the valuer's assessed value, not against what you negotiated, so a wide price-value gap can leave you funding a shortfall.
The rest of this course builds the three methods, comparable sales, income capitalization and replacement cost, that turn value from an opinion into a defensible number.

body.text: LTV slabs, stamp duty practices and valuer empanelment norms referenced in this lesson are indicative and can change with RBI, state government or IBBI updates, and with individual bank policy. Verify current norms with your lender or a registered valuer before relying on them for an actual transaction.
